messages.body_plain:
Hey,

Thanks for the message. So it looks like the variables "chrStart" and "chrEnd" are not being set properly (these variables tell STITCH where to start and stop reading the BAM). They are set in the function "initialize_chrStart_and_chrEnd" which sets "chrStart" based on the minimum position seen in the "posfile" in the region of interest, and similarly for chrEnd. I'm wondering if there are no SNPs in the imputation region? This would make sense given the warning message above. If this is the case I need to make STITCH throw better errors

Can you try running the following in R and let me know what you get

pos <- read.table("pos500.txt", header = FALSE, sep = "\t")
dim(pos)
range(pos[, 2], na.rm = TRUE)
range(pos[, 2], na.rm = FALSE)
L <- as.integer(as.character(pos[, 2]))
buffer=250000
regionStart=130000001
regionEnd=140000000
sum( ((regionStart - buffer) <= L) & (L < regionStart)) ## left region
sum( (regionStart <= L) & (L <= regionEnd)) ## interior region
sum( (regionEnd < L) & (L <= (regionEnd + buffer))) ## right region

Thanks,
Robbie

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I released version 1.5.2 of STITCH a few days ago. Changes compared to 1.5.1 include the following

1. Capability to substantially decrease RAM usage when running with a large number of samples

2. Better error message when imputing few or no SNPs

3. Able to impute when only 2 SNPs, including 1 SNP in central region

Details about release versions can be found at

https://github.com/rwdavies/STITCH/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md

Speed and performance benchmarks can he found at

https://github.com/rwdavies/STITCH/blob/master/benchmarks/summarize_benchmarking.md

The repo is at

https://github.com/rwdavies/STITCH

Best,

Robbie

Hi,

Looks like your job ran out of RAM during the writing part. For very large samples, you can use the parameter "outputSNPBlockSize" to control how many SNPs are written to disk at once, and hence how much RAM is used in the writing stage. Larger values of outputSNPBlockSize are written faster but use more RAM, so lowering it will reduce RAM. The default is set to 10000, but if you're running out of RAM, I would recommend dropping this to 1000 or 500 and seeing how it performs. Let me know!

Best,
Robbie
